hyperedges.label: Bronze Table Creation Flow
hyperedges.description: The complete flow for creating a Bronze Iceberg table: config is loaded, table contract is retrieved, partition spec is built from contract keys, GCS path is resolved, and catalog.create_table is called. This flow connects config, contracts, paths, partitioning, and catalog into a single coordinated operation.

hyperedges.label: Design Constraint Enforcement Pattern
hyperedges.description: The package enforces architectural boundaries through multiple mechanisms: pure library constraint (no ETL), catalog type restriction (file-based only), and schema delegation (domain schemas in consumers). These constraints work together to keep lakehouse_core focused.

hyperedges.label: CENACE Data Migration Pipeline
hyperedges.description: PEND and PML datasets from CENACE domain are migrated from consolidated Parquet to Bronze Iceberg tables via the bootstrap_bronze script, following the migration strategy phases. The table contracts govern the target structure.

hyperedges.label: Medallion Architecture (Raw/Bronze/Silver/Gold)
hyperedges.description: Four-zone data architecture pattern: raw (immutable source), bronze (minimal structure), silver (cleaned/normalized), gold (business-ready); defines the data maturity progression across the entire lakehouse

hyperedges.label: Lakehouse Consumer Ecosystem
hyperedges.description: Three external repos (data-pipeline, data-manager, revenue-models) all depend on phoenix_lakehouse as the single source of truth for contracts, paths, and catalog access; each handles a different stage of the data lifecycle

hyperedges.label: GCS Bucket Lifecycle (Active + Legacy)
hyperedges.description: Three GCS buckets in different lifecycle states: novagrid-lakehouse (canonical active), lakehouse_phoenix (frozen legacy archive), novogrid-workqueue (frozen legacy); unification plan governs migration from legacy to canonical

nodes.label: lakehouse_core
nodes.description: Core Python library providing contracts, configuration, catalog access, path helpers, and table management for the Iceberg + GCS lakehouse platform. Pure library with no ETL logic.

nodes.label: LakehouseConfig
nodes.description: Pydantic model for lakehouse configuration: bucket, prefix, zones dict, catalog dict, and tables dict (table contracts). Validated on load.

nodes.label: ConfigError
nodes.description: Custom exception raised for configuration errors (missing file, invalid YAML, duplicate table contracts).

nodes.label: get_lakehouse_config()
nodes.description: Loads and caches lakehouse configuration from configs/lakehouse.yaml and modular configs/tables/*.yaml files. Merges table contracts with main config taking precedence.

nodes.label: _load_table_contracts()
nodes.description: Internal function that loads modular table contracts from configs/tables/*.yaml, merges them, and detects duplicates.

nodes.label: get_iceberg_catalog()
nodes.description: Returns a cached PyIceberg SQL catalog instance configured from lakehouse.yaml. Sets PYICEBERG_LEGACY_CURRENT_SNAPSHOT_ID env var. Supports only SQL (SQLite) catalog type.

nodes.label: zone_prefix()
nodes.description: Returns the GCS prefix string for a given zone name (raw/bronze/silver/gold), using config zone mapping.

nodes.label: table_prefix()
nodes.description: Returns the GCS prefix for a table: {zone_prefix}{domain}/{table_base}/. Uses table contract to resolve domain.

nodes.label: get_full_gcs_path()
nodes.description: Returns the full GCS URI (gs://{bucket}/{table_prefix}) for Iceberg table storage location.

nodes.label: get_table_identifier()
nodes.description: Splits a dotted table name (e.g., 'bronze.pend') into a PyIceberg Identifier tuple (namespace, table_name).

nodes.label: get_table_contract()
nodes.description: Retrieves the table contract dict from config.tables for a given fully-qualified table name.

nodes.label: create_partition_spec()
nodes.description: Creates a PyIceberg PartitionSpec from a list of partition key names and a schema, using IdentityTransform. Partition field IDs start at 1000.

nodes.label: create_bronze_table()
nodes.description: Creates an Iceberg table in the catalog using the table contract, partition spec, and GCS location. Supports overwrite mode.

nodes.label: lakehouse_core.schemas
nodes.description: Provides PyIceberg type re-exports (Schema, NestedField, StringType, TimestampType, etc.). Domain-specific schemas belong in consuming repositories, not here.

nodes.label: lakehouse_core.schemas.master_schemas
nodes.description: Kept for backward compatibility. Re-exports Schema and NestedField. Explicitly states domain-specific schemas should not be defined here.

nodes.label: bootstrap_bronze.py
nodes.description: CLI script that migrates consolidated Parquet files into Bronze Iceberg tables. Reads parquet, converts Arrow schema to Iceberg, creates tables via lakehouse_core API, and appends data.

nodes.label: validate_table_contract.py
nodes.description: CLI validation script that checks table contracts against lakehouse standards: required fields (domain, zone, schema, partition_by), valid zones, naming conventions (lowercase snake_case), schema key conventions.

nodes.label: Table Contract
nodes.description: A YAML-defined metadata record for each Iceberg table specifying domain, zone, schema key, partition_by list, and optional description. Contracts are the core abstraction that consuming repos use to know table layout.

nodes.label: Medallion Zone Architecture
nodes.description: Four-zone data architecture: raw (immutable source), bronze (minimally transformed), silver (cleaned/normalized), gold (features/metrics/results). Zones map to GCS prefixes.

nodes.label: Modular Config Pattern
nodes.description: Table contracts are split into per-domain YAML files under configs/tables/ (cenace.yaml, weather.yaml, revenue.yaml) and auto-merged at load time. Main lakehouse.yaml takes precedence on conflicts.

nodes.label: GCS Storage Layout
nodes.description: GCS bucket gs://lakehouse_phoenix/ with top-level directories: iceberg/ (catalog metadata warehouse), raw/, bronze/, silver/, gold/. Each zone has domain subdirectories per table contract.

nodes.label: Pure Library Constraint
nodes.description: phoenix_lakehouse must be a pure library: no ETL, no APIs, no Prefect, no data processing. Only defines contracts and configuration. Consuming repos do the actual work.

nodes.label: File-Based Catalog Constraint
nodes.description: Only file-based/Hadoop-style Iceberg catalog on GCS is allowed. No BigQuery catalog. All metadata under gs://lakehouse_phoenix/iceberg/. BigQuery may be used as compute engine in consuming repos but not as catalog here.

nodes.label: PEND (Precios de Energia en Nodos Distribuidos)
nodes.description: CENACE energy prices by load zone. Schema: timestamp, zone, pz, pz_ene, pz_per, pz_cng, market, region. Partitioned by market/region/zone/year. ~100+ zones, hourly data.
nodes.norm_label: pend (precios de energia en nodos distribuidos)

nodes.label: PML (Precios Marginales Locales)
nodes.description: CENACE locational marginal prices by node. Schema: timestamp, node, pml, pml_ene, pml_per, pml_cng, market, region. Partitioned by market/region/node/year. Hourly data.

nodes.label: Lakehouse Migration Strategy
nodes.description: Four-phase migration: (1) Define contracts in lakehouse.yaml, (2) Migrate consolidated Parquet to Bronze Iceberg in GCS, (3) Upload raw data to GCS raw zone, (4) Update pipeline to write directly to Iceberg.

nodes.label: CENACE Domain
nodes.description: Mexican electricity market data domain. Contains PEND and PML datasets from CENACE (Centro Nacional de Control de Energia). Tables live under cenace/ subdirectory in each zone.

nodes.label: Consuming Repositories
nodes.description: Repositories that import lakehouse_core as a dependency: data-pipeline, data-manager, revenue-models. They define domain-specific schemas and perform actual ETL/processing.

nodes.label: Why Pure Library Design
nodes.description: phoenix_lakehouse is kept as a pure library to enforce separation of concerns: contracts/config here, ETL/processing in consuming repos. This prevents coupling between layout definitions and processing logic, allows independent versioning, and keeps the dependency tree minimal.

nodes.label: Why File-Based Catalog Over BigQuery
nodes.description: File-based/Hadoop catalog chosen over BigQuery catalog because: single source of truth stored in GCS, no external catalog service dependencies, all metadata portable under warehouse path, simpler operational model. BigQuery explicitly excluded from catalog role.

nodes.label: Why Modular Config Layout
nodes.description: Table contracts split per-domain for modularity (each domain self-contained), scalability (add domains without touching existing configs), maintainability (clear separation), and clean git diffs per domain.

nodes.label: Why Schemas Belong in Consuming Repos
nodes.description: Domain-specific schemas (PEND, PML column definitions) are defined in consuming repositories, not in lakehouse_core. This keeps the core library domain-agnostic and avoids forcing all consumers to update when one domain's schema changes.
nodes.norm_label: why schemas belong in consuming repos

nodes.label: Catalog Type Discrepancy (SQL vs Hadoop)
nodes.description: DESIGN_CONSTRAINTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md state 'hadoop' catalog type, but catalogs.py implementation only supports 'sql' (SQLite) catalog type. This is a discrepancy between documentation and code.

nodes.description: Process of migrating consolidated Parquet files from data_pipeline/data/ into Iceberg bronze tables in GCS; migration scripts live in data-pipeline repo

nodes.label: Storage as System of Record
nodes.description: Design principle: GCS + Iceberg is the system of record; compute engines (BigQuery, DuckDB, Spark) are disposable and interchangeable

nodes.label: No Hardcoded Paths
nodes.description: Design principle: no repo hardcodes GCS paths or schemas; all table definitions and layout live in lakehouse-core as the single source of truth

nodes.label: Pure Library Boundary
nodes.description: Design principle: phoenix_lakehouse is strictly a library providing contracts and definitions; no ETL, no Prefect, no API calls, no data writing; all operational logic belongs in consuming repos

nodes.label: Raw Data Preservation
nodes.description: Design principle: always keep a raw copy of source data (files and/or raw_payload) and treat bronze as minimally transformed; enables replay and debugging

nodes.label: Pinned Contract Authority
nodes.description: Design principle: consumers use phoenix_lakehouse through pinned versions (semver or date-based); upgrades are deliberate; worker snapshots are labeled artifacts with source revision metadata

nodes.label: Lakehouse Unification Plan
nodes.description: Strategic plan to unify all data paths around gs://novagrid-lakehouse as single canonical warehouse; freeze legacy buckets; standardize contract authority through pinned phoenix_lakehouse

nodes.label: BigQuery Not Used as Catalog
nodes.description: Explicit decision: BigQuery is not used as an Iceberg catalog in this repo; it may be used as a compute engine via BigLake/external tables in consuming repos; catalog uses file-based/SQL approach

nodes.label: Modular Table Contracts Pattern
nodes.description: Recommended approach: domain-specific YAML files in configs/tables/ rather than inline in lakehouse.yaml; scales better, clear git diffs, auto-merged by config loader

nodes.label: Naming Conventions
nodes.description: Standards: table names as {zone}.{table_name} in snake_case lowercase; domain names lowercase; schema keys as {table_name}_{zone}; partition keys must exist in schema

nodes.label: DuckDB
nodes.description: Optional local analytics engine for reading Iceberg/Parquet on GCS for quick modeling and exploration

nodes.label: BigQuery
nodes.description: Optional compute engine (not source of truth); accesses Iceberg tables via BigLake/external tables for ad-hoc SQL and dashboards

nodes.label: Prefect
nodes.description: Orchestration engine for running ETL flows; used in data-pipeline and data-manager repos, explicitly excluded from phoenix_lakehouse

hyperedges.description: The package enforces architectural boundaries through multiple mechanisms: pure library constraint (no ETL), catalog type restriction (file-based only), and schema delegation (domain schemas in consumers). These constraints work together to keep lakehouse_core focused.

hyperedges.label: CENACE Data Migration Pipeline
hyperedges.description: PEND and PML datasets from CENACE domain are migrated from consolidated Parquet to Bronze Iceberg tables via the bootstrap_bronze script, following the migration strategy phases. The table contracts govern the target structure.

hyperedges.label: Medallion Architecture (Raw/Bronze/Silver/Gold)
hyperedges.description: Four-zone data architecture pattern: raw (immutable source), bronze (minimal structure), silver (cleaned/normalized), gold (business-ready); defines the data maturity progression across the entire lakehouse

hyperedges.label: Lakehouse Consumer Ecosystem
hyperedges.description: Three external repos (data-pipeline, data-manager, revenue-models) all depend on phoenix_lakehouse as the single source of truth for contracts, paths, and catalog access; each handles a different stage of the data lifecycle

hyperedges.label: GCS Bucket Lifecycle (Active + Legacy)
hyperedges.description: Three GCS buckets in different lifecycle states: novagrid-lakehouse (canonical active), lakehouse_phoenix (frozen legacy archive), novogrid-workqueue (frozen legacy); unification plan governs migration from legacy to canonical
